title: Which packages a ranked request accepts

blocks.text: A city scores a handful of road-resurfacing packages by hand before it commits to a model. Each package has a value for every objective, for example `{"safety": 42.0, "cost": 3.1, "noise": -6.0}`. The council ranks the objectives and gives each one a sense and tolerances, as a list of levels in priority order:

The packages the council accepts are found level by level. At each level, take the best value $`\Gamma`$ of that objective **among the packages still accepted**, and keep only the packages within the allowed loss $`\delta = \max(\text{abs\_tol},\ \text{rel\_tol} \cdot |\Gamma|)`$ of it: at least $`\Gamma - \delta`$ for a maximized objective, at most $`\Gamma + \delta`$ for a minimized one.

Write `accepted(packages, levels)`. `packages` maps a package name to its values; return the sorted list of the names that survive every level. About ten lines; no solver is needed for a handful of packages.

cases.says: two levels with no tolerance keep the packages that are best on the first and, among those, best on the second
a 5% tolerance on the first level keeps packages within 5% of its best, and the second level chooses among them
the second level's best is the best of the packages the first level kept, not of every package
a minimized level with an absolute tolerance keeps values up to its best plus the tolerance
a maximized level whose best is negative allows a loss of its relative tolerance times the best's size

origin.section: A Relative Tolerance Follows the Scenario; an Absolute One Stays Put

concepts: applying ranked objectives with senses and tolerances level by level, each best taken among the plans still accepted
